title: Affine linearization identifies the specified units and ideal-module cokernels
statement: For any scheme X [def-pc-scheme] and j≥0, let e_j:E_(j+1)→E_j be the constructed inclusion of [lem-sc-reduction-units-power-inclusion], and let F_j be the constructed quasi-coherent module cokernel of [lem-sc-reduction-ideal-power-quotient]. There is an isomorphism coker(e_j) ≅ ULift((F_j)_et) of abelian sheaves on the small etale site of X [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. All cokernels and F_j are specified constructions.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and the following Claim; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: Put f=q_(N^(j+1)), g=q_(N^(j+2)), and r=kernel.ι(f) followed by g. The specified inclusion e from E_(j+1) to E_j followed by r is zero, since e followed by kernel.ι(f) is kernel.ι(g). For any k annihilated by r, lift k followed by kernel.ι(f) through kernel(g); cancellation against the monomorphism kernel.ι(f) proves that this lift factors k through e. Thus e is a kernel of r. Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_of_f_is_kernel and Exact.isColimitImage show that factorThruImage(r) is a cokernel of e. Uniqueness of cokernels gives coker(e) isomorphic to image(r).

On each affine open, N^(j+1) is contained in N, and the product N^(j+1) times N^(j+1) is contained in N^(j+2), by Ideal.pow_le_self and Ideal.pow_le_pow_right with j+2 at most 2j+2. The specified module quotient is quasi-coherent by the existing instance. Apply the general nil-ideal image linearization with I=N^(j+1), J=N^(j+2). Compose its isomorphism with the cokernel-to-image isomorphism from the first step. The module cokernel in that theorem is definitionally the specified reductionIdealPowerQuotient.
